newsitem.title: UK: World rubber trade group mulls arbitration role.
newsitem.headline: World rubber trade group mulls arbitration role.

text.p: The International Rubber Association (IRA), which groups most rubber trade organisations, plans to set up an arbitration centre to police the market.
IRA chairman Ng Kok Tee told Reuters on Friday an international authority was needed to deal with rubber trade disputes arising mainly from contractual defaults.
"The body will also exercise authority on the enforcement of arbitration awards meted out by various association members," he said at an international rubber forum here.
The high rubber prices of 1994/95 had been matched by defaults by origins and buyers. Ng said the discipline of the market has improved since then and contracts were being respected.
"But there is still room for improvement," he added.
"The IRA can play a more effective role in bringing about a healthier market in the future," he said.
Many of the defaults of 1994 and 1995 involved Thai exporters and Chinese buyers. Some had received no compensation for losses incurred.
The IRA groups 28 trade members. Ng said groups from Taiwan, Africa and India had signed up as members.
The Philippines and South Korea had also shown interest in joining.
